topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the course structure, target audience, and key learning objectives for the cancer biology lecture series.

topics.label: Biological concepts and experimental models of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concept of cancer as a breakdown in differentiation driven by genetic and epigenetic alterations alongside the methods and challenges of studying it in vitro.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and morphological progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the histological and gross biological features that distinguish benign growth from invasive and metastatic malignancy using clinical examples and colorectal progression.

topics.label: Tumor classification, nomenclature, and clinical morbidity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the naming conventions for benign and malignant neoplasms and the physical and physiological mechanisms by which they cause patient harm and mortality.

topics.label: Tumor incidence across populations and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the distribution and frequency of tumor types across human demographics, tissues, and diverse multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and cancer screening methods
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the rationale, histological basis, efficacy, and limitations of screening programs for early cancer detection across different organ systems.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the lecture closing and gives housekeeping reminders regarding upcoming practicals.
